question.leadin: Name these places identified with the Korean War.
question.text: The UN army eventually almost took the whole Korean Peninsula before being repelled as it was approaching this river that separates North Korea from China.
question.clue: The Friendship Bridge is the only remaining bridge over this river and connects the cities of Dandong and Sinujiu.

swap.text: In the Battle of Incheon [in-CHAHN], MacArthur led a surprise amphibious assault on Korean troops, leading the way for the UNC to recapture this city.
swap.clue: The Han River runs through this city, and it shares an administrative region with Gyeonggi Province and Incheon.

question.text: Soldiers from Ming China helped defend Korea from Japanese invasion at the end of the 16th century. During that conflict, Korean Admiral Yi utilized these crazy awesome vessels which received their name from the appearance caused by their armored decks.
question.clue: An earlier example of an ironclad warship was this type of ship developed by Admiral Yi Sun-sin to resist a 16th century Japanese invasion of Korea. Named for the shape of the animal on its bow, these ships boasted cannons and a hull covered in spikes.

swap.leadin: Name these dictators who are still alive.
swap.text: This man assumed leadership of North Korea in 1997. He has insisted on the right to nuclear power and oversaw the imprisonment of two American journalists last summer.
swap.clue: His "Sunshine policy" tried to bolster the software industry, and he once abducted a movie director to shoot a socialist Godzilla flick.

question.leadin: It was part of Operation Chromite.
question.text: Name this amphibious invasion and decisive U.N. victory during the Korean War in September 1950 that would allow for the subsequent retaking of the Kimpo airfield and the recapture of Seoul.
question.clue: Before this battle, allied troops bombed the Island of Wolmido .

swap.leadin: This amphibious landing was code-named Operation Chromite.
swap.text: Name this invasion carried out by UN forces during the Korean War to allow an advance from the Pusan Perimeter to retake Seoul.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of Incheon [or the Battle of Inchon; or Incheon Sangnyuk Jakjeon]

question.leadin: This leader's government was criticized for its lack of a public response to the sinking of the Sewol ferry.
question.text: Name this leader of the Saenuri Party, who became the first female head of state of any Eastern Asian country in 2013. Her dictatorial father ruled over the Third and Fourth Republics from 1963-79.
question.answerHtml: Park Geun-hye [do not accept or prompt on “Park Chung-hee”]

swap.text: During the war, U.N. pilots also referred to the northwest of Korea as "[these planes] Alley," since Americans F-86 Sabres often encountered Soviet aircraft there.
swap.clue: During the war, the northwest of North Korea gained this nickname from UN forces, due to the presence of Soviet fighter planes here. Along the Yalu River, this region was the site of many dogfights.

question.leadin: Among this man's domestic accomplishments include granting serfs a form of maternity leave and backing the development of the world's first rain gauge.
question.text: Identify this fourth ruler of Korea's Joseon (JOH-sun) dynasty whose establishment of the 28-letter hangul script is still celebrated on an October holiday.
question.clue: This king implemented the Hall of Worthies, which produced a replacement to Hanja that only has 28 letters.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Asian dynasties.
swap.text: Ending with the Japanese annexation in 1910, this dynasty ruled Korea for over five hundred years from the capital Hanyang, and it saw the creation of the Hangul phonetic alphabet.
swap.clue: It attempted to curb the power of its scholar officials in four "literati purges," and eventually its ruling intelligentsia devolved into the Sirhak and Tonghak movements.

question.leadin: This kingdom eventually conquered the Baekje and Goguryeo kingdoms, ending the Three Kingdoms Period.
question.text: Name this ancient kingdom of South Korea that ruled much of the southern part of the Korean peninsula during the first millennium.
question.clue: This kingdom included the hereditary "head rank 6" caste in its "bone rank" system, and used highly-educated elite knights whose name means "flower boys."

swap.text: Both the Korean War and the Pueblo incident were ended by negotiations in this central Korean village on the Kyongui road.
swap.clue: This village which hosted a more famous conference that led to the armistice between United Nations forces and communists in 1953 during the Korean War.

question.leadin: This naval commander destroyed approximately 100 enemy ships at the Battle of Hansan Island without losing a single ship of his own.
question.text: Name this admiral who leveraged the regular reversal of the tide to win the Battle of Myeongnyang ("myung-nyahng"). This undefeated Korean admiral used turtle ships to defend Korea during the Imjin War.

swap.leadin: In 1866, France occupied this island for six weeks following the execution of seven Catholic missionaries during a crackdown on Christians initiated by Heungseon Daewongun.
swap.text: Name this island, where the Japanese ship Un'yo provoked a battle that led to an 1876 unequal treaty named for it. That treaty named for this island ended the Joseon Kingdom's status as a tributary of the Qing Dynasty.

question.text: Under Yang, China attempted to conquer this kingdom, which opposed Baekje and Silla during the Korean Three Kingdoms Period. That invasion failed after the Battle of the Salsu River.
question.clue: This first native Korean state arose near the Yalu River in the first century CE and conquered the Chinese colony of Lolang.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about early fighting in the Korean War - er, "police action."
swap.text: The Eighth Army set about defending a "perimeter" named for this South Korean Port city.
swap.clue: Following the North's seizure of Seoul, this city became the temporary capital of the Republic of Korea. Its namesake "perimeter" was attacked by General Kim Chaek.

question.text: In 935, General Wang Kon overthrew the Silla Kingdom to establish this successor state, which ruled the peninsula until 1392 and produced valuable celadon ceramics.

swap.text: Original language term required. The Hanjungrok claims that Crown Prince Sado suffered from a "phobia" of this clothing, often burning many outfits. Modern examples of this traditional class of clothing were modeled on Joseon-era outfits.

question.leadin: In interviews after this event, an American participant claimed he was pushed to give a statement that he "understood why the United States was scared."
question.text: Name this two day event held in 1995 whose chief international promoter, Antonio Inoki, hyped it up to honor his teacher Rikidozan.
question.answerHtml: Collision in Korea [or Pyongyang International Sports and Culture Festival for Peace]

swap.leadin: Early 20th century ultranationalist historian Shin Chaeho denounced this text for disregarding Manchurian kingdoms as ethnically-Korean, and affirming an ideology of servitude to China called sadaejuui.
swap.text: Name this 12th century text compiled by Kim Busik, the oldest extant chronicle of Korean history. A later text describes the "memorabilia" or yusa of the same era of history that this book records.
